newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt mkts close firmer, bills buoyed by NZ dlr.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt mkts close firmer, bills buoyed by NZ dlr.

text.p: New Zealand debt securities closed mostly firmer on Thursday, with the short end in particular underpinned by a strong New Zealand dollar.

"Obviously the market's feeling fairly good about the currency. The TWI's remaining fairly high -- if the offshore guys were going to sell it over the last few days, there's been plenty of opportunity," a bill dealer said.
The New Zealand dollar firmed in early trade but had drifted back to US$0.7057/64 and 67.28 on its Trade-Weighted Index by the close.
The 90-day bank bill yield ended four points lower at 7.96 percent while the 90-day bill futures contract firmed eight points to 92.61.
"There still is a lot of cash mulling around in the forwards market, coming out of Asia, so that's why yields are a little bit lower -- a bit of a cash-led rally," the dealer said.
Although volume had been light in the long end, the bond market also firmed slightly.
"It tried to sell off first thing this morning but it's come back fairly well bid," a dealer said.
The 11/06 bond yield fell two points to 7.42 percent.
"The curve is showing a little bit of interest in steepening with a bit of interest in the longer end. It's not substantial but we've seen a little bit of it today," said the dealer.
Little movement was expected in the long end over the Christmas period, but the money market was seen reasonably active.

"Over Christmas we're still going to have quite a lot of cash coming through and the Asian market looking to invest. That mixed with a thin market should probably still be a relatively well bid market," said one dealer.
